claims.summary: The burst-and-rest loop tapers warmth at rest entry and changes rest duration according to observed fill.
claims.disposition: Verified from the exact report-bound source. Rest entry uses a 0.7-to-0.4 taper and a 0.50-to-0.35 warmth blend; fill below 30% maps to max(floor(0.6 * base_rest), 30). This verifies code shape, not felt effect.

claims.summary: The final burst-to-first-rest change should be measured and checked against a proposed threshold below 0.3.
claims.disposition: A new read-only audit establishes that the exact pair is unavailable. The first rest pulse initializes previous_rest_features to none, and the status contains no final burst vector, so the cross-boundary threshold remains unverified rather than being replaced with another metric.

claims.summary: Existing rest observations may still describe how consecutive pulses vary after entry.
claims.disposition: The durable bounded live capture found one complete rest episode and nine intra-rest comparisons, all observed delta_rms values below 0.3 with maximum 0.1061888262629509. This is explicitly intra-rest evidence only and does not establish the missing boundary pair, felt smoothness, safety, or relief.

claims.summary: At 25% fill, ten rest-duration evaluations should show whether the shortening branch prevents further fill loss.
claims.disposition: The deterministic ten-point envelope proves scheduling only: nominal bases 45-90 map to 30-54 seconds, while current RNG-reachable bases 45-67 map to 30-40 seconds. The live window contained no rest samples at or below 30% fill, so recovery and causation remain unobserved.

claims.summary: Warmth-vector details and base-rest variance could affect the transition texture.
claims.disposition: Verified as a reason not to fabricate a deterministic cross-boundary claim. craft_warmth_vector contains stochastic microtexture and the rest path can blend encoded journal features, spectral feedback, and gesture seed. The audit reports only available observations and scheduling math.

claims.summary: Changing warmth, cadence, fill regulation, scheduling, controller behavior, or live signals would be a substrate-facing intervention.
claims.disposition: Preserved as a Tier 5 Mike/operator approval wait. The new audit is read-only and all cadence, fill, scheduling, controller, signal, felt-cause, safety, relief, and approval authority markers remain false.
